deep.reconstruction:
The page is a table of decimal periods, continuing from the previous page (571, 569, 563, ... 521) and the next page (479, 467, ...). For each prime p (509, 503, 499, 491, 487) Gauss writes the repeating decimal digits of 1/p. He writes them in groups of ten and in rows of seven groups. He starts at the first nonzero digit, so the leading '00' of 0.00... is dropped. He keeps writing until the start of the period visibly recurs, then marks the break with '....'.

(1) p = 509. 1/509 = 0.(001964636542 2396856581 ...).
- Written digits: 7·70 + 20 = 510.
- The final group 0216110019 ends with '0019', which is the start of the period again. So the period is 508 = p−1 digits, ending in ...021611.
- Last-digit check (mine): 509·x ≡ −1 (mod 10) gives x = 1. ✓

(2) p = 503. 1/503 = 0.(001988071570 ...).
- 510 digits are written. The final group 0019880715 is an exact repeat of the first ten period digits.
- Period 502 = p−1, ending ...9662027833.
- Last-digit check: 503·3 = 1509 ≡ 9 (mod 10), so the last digit is 3. ✓

(3) p = 499. 1/499 = 0.(002004008016032064 ...). Because 499 = 500 − 1, the leading digits double: 002, 004, 008, 016, ...
- 500 digits are written. The final group 2505010020 ends with '0020', the repeat of the start.
- Period 498, ending ...250501.

(4) p = 491. 1/491 = 0.(002036659877 ...).
- 490 digits are written. The final group 8329938900 ends with '00', the repeat.
- Period 490, ending ...83299389.
- Last-digit check: 491·9 ≡ 9 (mod 10), so the last digit is 9. ✓

(5) p = 487. 1/487 = 0.(002053388090 ...).
- 490 digits are written. The final group 7577002053 ends with '002053', the repeat.
- Period 486, ending ...7577.
- Last-digit check: 487·7 ≡ 9 (mod 10). ✓

In every case the period length is p−1. So 10 is a primitive root modulo 509, 503, 499, 491 and 487; these are 'full reptend' primes.

My own consistency checks (implicit, not on the page). For a full period of length p−1, digit k and digit k+(p−1)/2 sum to 9 (Midy's theorem, which follows from 10^{(p−1)/2} ≡ −1 mod p). I applied this to the doubtful places. In each case the complement of the matching earlier digits reproduces the written group exactly:
- 509: offset 254, used for groups 1964636542, 5579567779 and 4734774066.
- 503: offset 251, group 5009940357.
- 499: offset 249, groups 6152304609 and 2184368737.
- 491: offset 245, the blotted final group 8329938900.
- 487: offset 243, the tail 7577.

Purpose: this is part of Gauss's large manuscript table converting fractions with prime denominators below 1000 into decimals. It is the computational counterpart of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae arts. 312–318 (periods of decimal fractions and their use with indices/primitive roots). Each prime is written as a single full period; by Gauss's method the periods of a/p are then read off as cyclic shifts.
errors: No arithmetic errors detected. The overwritten or corrected digits in the 509 block (groups 5579567779 and 4734774066) and the blotted start of the last 491 group are consistent with the complementary-half check, so the corrected readings are right.
